title: sub: p1-structured-output
creator: codex
notes:
S1 in progress on feat/p1d-structured-output. Ticket scope: the main chain moves to provider-native structured output + Pydantic schema + semantic validator + validation-error retry; _parse_json_response_impl becomes a legacy fallback; ContentPlan and friends get typed. Reconnaissance (2026-09-15): 25 _parse_json_response call sites across 13 agents, a second copy in services/llm_enrichment.py, zero with_structured_output anywhere, and three definitions of the same concept (api/generated Pydantic contract, state TypedDict, agent-side dicts). Production routes 13/15 TaskTypes to astron-code-latest (XUNFEI) and 4 of the 6 providers are OpenAI-compatible endpoints, so native structured-output support cannot be verified offline. Confirmed with the user before implementing: (1) capability declaration + degradation chain rather than all-native, (2) a new LLM-facing output model with normalisation rather than reusing the generated contract (too strict for a model: AwareDatetime / hex pattern / StrictStr would fail legal output), (3) this slice = scaffolding + one pilot (content_strategist ContentPlan). Red lines: no prompt text change (P1b snapshot stays at 0 drift), no edits under api/generated, no new dependency, _parse_json_response behaviour untouched. S1 landed on feat/p1d-structured-output (2026-09-15). Shipped: structured.py (capability declaration per provider, overridable via XHS_STRUCTURED_MODE_<PROVIDER>; degradation_path; validate_output doing schema only; StructuredOutputError), outputs.py (permissive ContentPlanOutput + normalize_content_plan), base.py _llm_structured / _structured_call / _llm_ainvoke(runnable, model_kwargs, raw unwrap), and the content_strategist pilot migration. Four things only surfaced once it ran: (1) the old drift guard nudged once and then accepted, so plumbing it through a fail-fast chain silently promoted an advisory check to a hard requirement -> added accept_last_valid (malformed payloads are still never returned; only validator refusals can be); (2) validate_output collapsed schema failure and validator refusal into one return value, which is the same trap -> it now does schema only and the caller runs the validator; (3) the NATIVE level was dead, because with_structured_output returns a validated instance and validate_output demanded a dict -> it now accepts a mapping or an instance of output_model; (4) the leniency branches in outputs.py were unreachable behind list[str] fields, and a model writing "a、b" for key_points would have been iterated character by character -> shape leniency moved into the model via mode=before validators and _as_list. Also fixed an existing defect found on the way: builder.py's content_strategist conditional edge omitted "__end__" from its path map while content_strategist_router returns it from its terminal guard, so any content_strategist failure crashed the graph with KeyError: '__end__' (fixed, plus tests/unit/graph/test_conditional_edge_wiring.py which compares every router's Literal return set against its path map both ways). Gates: pytest 2868 passed / 3 skipped, ruff check + format clean (491 files), mypy clean (199 files), P1b baseline drift 0, tool_runtime_gate OK. S2a landed on feat/p1d-s2a-scout-agents (2026-09-15). Scout agents first: trend_scout (SCOUTING -> XUNFEI -> PROMPTED) and blogger_scout (MOCK_GEN -> DEEPSEEK -> JSON_OBJECT), which between them cover both non-native levels and are the only two agents on the JSON_OBJECT level. Shipped: outputs.py (7 new models for TrendData / BloggerProfile plus normalize_trend_data / normalize_blogger_candidates, helpers _as_float dropping the percent sign without rescaling, _as_int reading "5万"/"1.2w"/"3k", _topic_text settling the topic/title/name/keyword aliases once), structured.py (render_schema_instructions recursing into nested models once each, _type_label learning Any and Optional[X]), both agents migrated onto _llm_structured, and _retry_mock_with_explicit_json deleted (36 lines, no test referenced it, and the facility retries with a correction on its own). Three things only surfaced once it ran: (1) THE EXPENSIVE ONE — _llm_structured treated "could not ask" as "answered badly": a call that raised was recorded as "this level is unusable" and the chain degraded, so a complete LLM outage became empty trends with a success status, taking 07-07's error state and P1a-S2's failed perf entries with it and turning three test_stateful_retry E2E tests red. Judged class (b) — a real regression — and fixed in the facility: when the chain is exhausted and not one level ever answered, the original exception is raised instead of StructuredOutputError. The distinction carries weight because StructuredOutputError is what callers convert into a business fallback ("no trends this time"), and an outage that borrows that meaning is an outage nobody retries. (2) _parse_json_response's failure payload {"raw_content": ...} now PASSES the schema (every field has a default, extras are ignored), so keeping the model's text out of state rests on the output model declaring every key rather than on the chain refusing it — both mechanisms hold, and the assertion pins the property rather than one mechanism. (3) the schema hint did not spell out nested models, which is exactly the shape the scouts return; added the recursion and fixed Optional[X] being labelled "string" — with expand-once that mislabel has no compensating expansion. Pre-existing defects found on the way: trending_notes and market_saturation are read by blogger_scout and content_strategist but were never declared on TrendData (now modelled, with a test pinning the remaining gap to exactly those two keys); and six test_blogger_scout cases used AsyncMock() as the model, whose bind() returns an un-awaited coroutine, so the JSON_OBJECT level died with AttributeError and the chain silently degraded to PROMPTED — green tests that never ran the level production uses (replaced with a real double plus a bound == [{"response_format": {"type": "json_object"}}] assertion). Gates: pytest 2910 passed / 3 skipped, ruff check + format clean (493 files), mypy clean (199 files), P1b baseline drift 0, tool_runtime_gate OK. S2b landed on feat/p1d-s2b-analysis-agents (2026-09-15). Ticket scope: the remaining astron-code-latest main-chain agents. Reconnaissance found 6 call sites across 5 agents (brief_analyzer x2, analyst, content_analyzer, viral_matcher) plus an S1 leftover in content_strategist.py:420 (the low-viral re-generation). evaluator is deliberately held back as S2c: it is the only call site that already has a deterministic re-computation builder (_build_evaluation_result, ~250 lines) and a degraded path, so migrating it means rewriting existing logic rather than replacing a parser. Shipped: 11 output models + 6 normalisers in outputs.py (__all__ 8 -> 21) covering brief / clarification / analytics / gap analysis / viral references; accepts_bare_list plus a shape-aware correction in structured.py; all 6 call sites on _llm_structured, which clears the last S1 leftover. The load-bearing finding: validate_output refused every non-object root, but _parse_json_response really does return a list for [{"field": ...}] (measured, not assumed) and two old call sites accepted both spellings - so a literal migration would have turned "accepted" into "hard failure". The facility gap had to be closed first: a model declares accepts_bare_list via ClassVar and validate_output admits the array, and the correction text is derived from the same predicate, because telling a model that takes a question list that its answer "must be an object" spends the retry narrowing it to the spelling we did not need. Degradation policy was decided per call site from its observable consequences rather than copied: brief_analyzer degrades on StructuredOutputError (an empty parse has confidence 0.5 < 0.6, so the brief still goes to the user - the old behaviour, now explicitly named), analyst and content_analyzer degrade the same way but let "never answered" propagate (an empty analytics snapshot carries views=0 / engagement_rate=0.0 into state and the report, indistinguishable from a post that really got nothing - P1c's "all zeroes are not data" one layer up), and viral_matcher keeps catching everything because its output is optional and the failure is labelled (optimization_error) rather than disguised. Also fixed: test_viral_matcher's timeout case was falsely green - MagicMock invents bind() returning a non-awaitable, so the JSON_OBJECT level died of a double-manufactured TypeError and the chain (which re-raises the first level's failure) reported that instead of the timeout; replaced with a real stand-in. One observation left unfixed: raise unreachable[0][1] surfaces the first level's exception even when the levels fail differently, and no existing test can distinguish first from last, so the choice deserves its own round. Gates: pytest 2965 passed / 3 skipped, ruff 491 files clean, mypy 199 files clean, P1b baseline drift 0, tool runtime gate OK. S2c migrated the evaluator's single LLM call site onto the structured chain (feat/p1d-s2c-evaluator). Unlike S2a/S2b this payload is not state: it is the read-only input to _build_evaluation_result, which recomputes overall_score/decision/coverage from fixed rules, so EvaluationPanelOutput declares only the half a model may state (dimensions/revision_hints/summary/bias_warning) and deliberately does not model overall_score/decision -- the prompt's example asks the model for both, and extra=ignore is what makes those land instead of rule. The builder and all three pre-existing degraded paths are byte-identical. The expensive finding: 'prose gets stopped by the schema' is false. _parse_json_response never fails on prose, it returns {'raw_content': ...}, and for a model whose every field has a default that is a legal dict, so validate_output refused nothing and the pre-migration behavior survived -- a prose answer produced status=partial with degraded=False, byte-identical to a panel that honestly covered part of the table. The semantic check (_panel_has_dimensions) became load-bearing the moment a probe showed this, not as optional hardening; it corrects once, and exhausting the chain lands on an explicit degraded exit symmetric with the timeout branch (_panel_unavailable_result, one shared factory) because both are the same physical event and the router already sends a decision-less result to the human channel. A third failure still propagates: when no level can be called at all, _llm_structured re-raises the original exception, which is also the pre-migration behavior via _llm_ainvoke. Two deliberate behavior changes recorded: bool('false') used to read a model-declared-unavailable dimension as available and score it (now False), and the three-state available (absent vs explicit null) is preserved through normalisation because the bool(...) that flattens them already owns that job downstream. Second process finding: the mutation self-check must rewrite the original file before each mutation -- the first round accumulated nine mutations on one file, so after M1 removed the validator argument M3's edit no longer reached any executed path and reported a false green; per-mutation reset killed 9/9. Gates: pytest 2987 passed / 3 skipped, ruff check + format 491 files clean, mypy 199 files clean, P1b baseline drift 0, tool runtime gate OK.

P1d-S3 (writing agents) landed. Eight output models (CopyContentOutput; a private _ContentVersionFields base with StyleVariantOutput/ContentVersionOutput subclasses; StyleVariantsOutput; ContentVersionsOutput; VisualPlanOutput; ShootingAngleOutput; ShootingPlanOutput) plus five normalisers, and six call sites across copywriter, version_generator (two structurally identical blocks folded into one _write_versions helper), visual_designer and shooting_planner. All four task types route to the XUNFEI-compatible endpoint, so every call site validates on the PROMPTED level only and the corrective retry is the whole recovery mechanism. Dispositions split by what an empty result would look like: the three whose MAIN product is the payload (copywriter main draft, visual_designer, shooting_planner) carry a semantic validator and let the failure travel to BaseAgent.__call__'s error state, because their empty payload is byte-for-byte indistinguishable from a real empty observation -- for shooting_planner it collides exactly with its own early return of an empty shooting_plan. The two collection products (style variants, A/B/C versions) use advisory validators (accept_last_valid) so the old zero-item outcome stays reachable; the retry that used to be hand-rolled verbatim now carries a correction. Two design reversals recorded. First, the two version models share a base class after all: content_versions has one set of readers (choice_gate, artifacts, the OMP tool, the frontend) that do not distinguish the source, so the two field sets must be isomorphic and a base class is the only place that invariant can live. Second, the contract-only keys (image_prompts/changes_summary/predicted_score) leave ONLY when the model wrote them, decided with model_fields_set: downstream reads the omission itself (omp_bridge falls back to the literal string draft, artifacts to 0.0), so emitting a default would delete the placeholder from every existing version. Also recorded: the state contract and the prompts drift in both directions (VisualPlan declares layout_style that no prompt writes while omitting visual_style/layout_preference; ContentVersion omits version_type/tone/visual_style/color_palette). The payload reproduces the prompt's shape as before -- reconciling the drift would change what existing readers see -- and it is pinned as a two-way set difference so either half going away turns red. Process finding: mutation M4 survived and exposed an untested path. Prose is schema-legal and is absorbed by accept_last_valid, so the except branch only runs when the schema itself refuses (a bare array), which had no test; adding one made it 12/12 killed. Gates: pytest 3020 passed / 3 skipped, ruff check + format 492 files clean, mypy 199 files clean, P1b baseline drift 0, tool runtime gate OK.

S4 (feat/p1d-s4-legacy-parser): converged the legacy text->JSON parsing strategy into a single home, backend/models/json_parsing.py::parse_json_payload (UNPARSED sentinel on total failure), with BaseAgent._parse_json_response_impl reduced to a thin sentinel wrapper (both warning strings preserved verbatim) and both legacy entry points documented as LEGACY. Finding #1: _parse_json_response is NOT leftover — its only runtime caller is _structured_call, i.e. it IS the PROMPTED/JSON_OBJECT tier parser on the production hot path (13/15 TaskTypes resolve to PROMPTED); it may only be deleted once only NATIVE_SCHEMA remains. Finding #2 (probe overturned the design assumption): the llm_enrichment parser is NOT a copy — an 18-case probe shows 5 entries with different accept sets and neither side is a superset (base has _repair_json for unquoted hashtags, the copy has a greedy array rescue), and base silently truncates an array embedded in prose to its first element. Merging either way would change the other side's behaviour, which the topic red line forbids, so S4 deliberately does NOT merge and instead pins the divergence as executable assertions (TestTheTwoParsersCannotBeMerged) plus pins the known defect as 'do not fix in this slice'. The failure contract is load-bearing: the sentinel is a valid dict (invisible to extra="ignore" models, S2c), while the copy's raise is the only thing that triggers fallback_fn in enrich_with_llm (de_ai_taste depends on method == "algorithmic"). Behaviour preservation is proven by a byte-identical before/after probe diff plus three agent-boundary tests. Gates: pytest 3065 passed / 3 skipped (+45, exactly the new file's cases, so no existing test was touched), ruff check + format 494 files clean, mypy 200 files clean, P1b baseline drift 0, tool runtime gate OK, mutation self-check 6/6 killed (including the 'just converge it' mutation and the 'just fix it' defect mutation).
